case.believed: AtomicLong deserialization of numeric strings and floating-point tokens is equivalent to integral-token deserialization, so values outside the 32-bit range cannot be silently narrowed on a 64-bit target.
contract: A numeric string above Integer.MAX_VALUE deserializes to AtomicLong without 32-bit truncation.
A floating-point token above Integer.MAX_VALUE follows the default ACCEPT_FLOAT_AS_INT policy, drops only its fractional part, and preserves the 64-bit integral value.
A negative numeric string below Integer.MIN_VALUE preserves its negative 64-bit value.
A large integral token remains a full-width AtomicLong baseline, and an AtomicLong bean property uses the same corrected string-coercion path.
Disabling ACCEPT_FLOAT_AS_INT rejects floating-point input instead of silently coercing it.
Configuring integer String coercion to Fail rejects a quoted number instead of bypassing the policy.
case.goal: Prove Jackson Databind 2.21.4 preserves 64-bit AtomicLong values on coerced string and floating-point paths fixed in this patch, while still honoring strict coercion settings.
